scenario_description:
Objective: Gain authentic audience exposure and editorial feedback by using a ready, original rain-garden note in an optional teaching-digest feature.
Emerging Need: The publication route remains unusable while the issue theme is unsettled; a locked rain-garden theme and an unfilled aerenchyma capsule later make the saved note a precise fit.
Decision Context: Format, rights, delivery address, and production cutoff are public, while the stored note’s provenance, publication preference, and linked portfolio item determine whether participation is suitable.
Consequence: Selection could strengthen a portfolio and add named credit; letting the layout close leaves the course item, grades, and certificate progress unchanged.

parameter.subject: Personal field-log receipt: rain-garden capsule
parameter.body:
Personal portfolio record for HORT-226: this is my completed March26 field observation and original capsule, saved for review.
Working title: Air spaces at the rain-garden edge
Species: Juncus effusus (soft rush)
Observation site: College teaching rain garden
Observation date: 2026-03-26
Capsule: At the college teaching rain garden, soft rush remained upright in saturated soil after overnight rain. A fallen stem showed a pale, airy pith rather than a solid core. Those connected air spaces are aerenchyma: they move oxygen from exposed shoots toward tissues in oxygen-poor, waterlogged soil. The tissue does not remove flooding, but it helps living cells keep respiring when gas diffusion through wet soil is slow. This internal ventilation helps explain why soft rush occupies the basin edge where several neighboring upland species thin out.
Provenance: Leona's own field observation and wording; no classmate material.
Publication preference: One-issue, non-exclusive college-digest permission with name credit is acceptable; retain course-use rights.

parameter.subject: Plant-in-Place April issue: theme vote and contribution rules
parameter.body: The April teaching digest is deciding between Rain-garden adaptations and Alpine survival; the theme vote will be final at noon Wednesday. Standing rules allow unsolicited original student field-note capsules only after the theme is locked. Capsules must be 120 words or fewer and include species, site, and observation date. Delivery for eligible text is by email to this sender. Accepted pieces receive a brief editor note and named credit unless anonymity is requested, under a one-issue, non-exclusive permission.

parameter.title: Plant-in-Place April layout export
parameter.description: Program-feed production milestone. The issue theme locks at 12:00. Eligible capsules matching the locked theme can be considered until the 16:00 layout export; no additions are possible afterward.

parameter.content: The rain-garden theme is now locked. I can see the final spread list from the editorial crew: its only unfilled field-note box is the 120-word explanation of aerenchyma in a plant observed in waterlogged soil; the other adaptation boxes already have copy. The layout is still scheduled to export at 16:00.

parameter.subject: April teaching-digest layout exported
parameter.body: The April layout was exported at 16:00. No further field-note capsules can be added to this issue.
